newsitem.title: USA: Bank of New York seeks to raise State Street stake.
newsitem.headline: Bank of New York seeks to raise State Street stake.

text.p: Bank of New York said it was seeking approval from the Federal Reserve Board and the Massachusetts Board of Bank Incorporation to raise its stake in State Street Boston Corp to 9.9 percent from 4.99 percent.

Analysts and stock traders said the announcement that Bank of New York had quietly built a stake in State Street and wanted to increase it, looked like the beginning of a courtship that could eventually lead to a full scale takeover.
One analyst said a 4.99 percent was an investment but a stake twice that size as proposed by Bank of New York was something more.

Bank of New York said as of Sept. 30, it held 4.99 percent of State Street Boston Corp's 80.1 million shares outstanding. Bank of New York said in a statement after the stock market closed that the objective of the increased holding was for investment purposes.
State Street Boston said in a statement that the company was committed to delivering long term value for shareholders, and its board believes the company should remain independent.
With $52.4 billion in assets as of Sept. 30, Bank of New York ranked as the 16th-largest U.S. bank holding company.
State Street Boston provides services for management of financial assets and has about $2.7 trillion of assets under custody and $280 billion of assets under management.

Analyst George Salem of Gerard Klauer Mattison said if Bank of New York was intent on pursuing a full-fledged merger with State Street Boston, "it certainly makes all the sense in the world.". He said, "The businesses overlap greatly and there would be a ton of cost saves in the processing business."

Analysts noted that the interest by Bank of New York in State Street Boston reflected the view that securities processing has high profit margins compared to some other banking activities and is a stable business.
Securities processing includes services such as custody, settlement of trades, proxy management and and pricing and performance analysis for securties portfolios.

Bank of New York has been stepping up its activities in securities processing. At the company's shareholders meeting in May, Chairman J. Carter Bacot said the company found the profit margins attractive in processing businesses.

A Bank of New York spokesman, when asked if there had been any talks between Bank of New York and State Street Boston about the stake, declined coment. He did say that Bank of New York has owned the stock since the third quarter of 1995 and State Street Boston has been aware of it for at least six months.
State Street Boston's stock fell $1.625 to $63 and Bank of New York fell edged down 50 cents to $33.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
